LESSON: DEVELOPMENT OF TRANSPORT

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Resources and Economic Activities
Topic 3.5: Development of Transport
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Development of Transport, part of Resources and Economic Activities in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we use our roads safely? 2. How can one avoid accidents on the road?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Development of Transport together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: speaks and signs clearly as learners identify modern means of communication such as mobile

phones, internet, television, radio and newspapers using appropriate media.

● Creativity and Imagination: undertake group activities as learners role-play use of various modern means of communication.

Values:
● Unity: team spirit as learners discuss in groups, causes of road accidents in Kenya and share in class.

● Peace: love for their own community as learners role play how to observe traffic rules while using the road.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Nationalism: national pride when visiting a nearby children’s traffic park to learn more about road safety.

• Child road safety: learners work harmoniously in discussions in groups, causes of road accidents in Kenya and share in class.

Link to other subjects:

● English and Kenyan Sign Language: as learners in pairs brainstorm and sign the meaning of the term transport and share in class.

Suggested Learning Resources:

print resources, digital resources, drawing materials, signed audio visual clips on ways of reducing accidents, KSL Dictionary,
